senses.def: to make sth unable to work so that it cannot be used

ex.en: The burglars gained entry to the building after disabling the alarm.
ex.cn: 窃贼破坏警报器后便得以进入大楼。

senses.def: unable to use a part of your body completely or easily because of a physical condition, an illness, an injury, etc.; unable to learn easily
senses.chn: 丧失能力的；有残疾的；无能力的

ex.en: physically/mentally disabled
ex.cn: 有生理残疾的；精神伤残的

ex.en: severely disabled
ex.cn: 严重伤残

ex.en: He was born disabled.
ex.cn: 他天生残疾。

ex.en: facilities for disabled people
ex.cn: 残疾人使用的设施

ex.en: mentally disabled
ex.cn: 精神伤残的

ex.en: learning disabilities
ex.cn: 学习障碍

senses.def: people who are disabled

ex.en: caring for the sick, elderly and disabled
ex.cn: 关心老弱病残

senses.def: the state of being disabled or the process of becoming disabled

ex.en: The insurance policy covers sudden death or disablement.
ex.cn: 保险单为突然死亡或伤残保险。

senses.def: to tell sb that what they think is true is, in fact, not true
senses.chn: 去掉（某人）的错误想法；使省悟

senses.def: something that causes problems and tends to stop sb/sth from succeeding or making progress
senses.chn: 不利因素；障碍；不便之处

ex.en: a serious/severe/considerable disadvantage
ex.cn: 重大的不利条件

ex.en: One major disadvantage of the area is the lack of public transport.
ex.cn: 这个地区的一大不便之处就是缺少公共交通工具。

ex.en: There are disadvantages to the plan.
ex.cn: 这个计划有诸多不利因素。

ex.en: What's the main disadvantage?
ex.cn: 主要的不利条件是什么？

ex.en: I was at a disadvantage compared to the younger members of the team.
ex.cn: 与队里较年轻的队员相比，我处于不利地位。

ex.en: The fact that he didn't speak a foreign language put him at a distinct disadvantage.
ex.cn: 他不会说外语使他处于明显的不利地位。

senses.def: not having the things, such as education, or enough money, that people need in order to succeed in life
senses.chn: 弱势的；社会地位低下的

ex.en: disadvantaged groups/children
ex.cn: 生活条件差的群体／孩子

ex.en: a severely disadvantaged area
ex.cn: 极贫困地区

ex.en: They were too poor to buy shoes for the kids.
ex.cn: 他们穷得没钱给孩子买鞋穿。

ex.en: socially disadvantaged sections of the community
ex.cn: 该社区社会地位低下的贫困阶层

ex.en: It's a charity that provides help for needy children.
ex.cn: 这是一个为贫困孩子提供援助的慈善机构。

ex.en: Thousands of impoverished peasants are desperate to move to the cities.
ex.cn: 成千上万赤贫的农民急切盼望搬到城里去。

senses.def: people who are disadvantaged
causing sb to be in a worse situation compared to other people

ex.en: The deal will not be disadvantageous to your company.
ex.cn: 这项交易不会对你公司不利。

senses.def: no longer satisfied with your situation, organization, belief, etc. and therefore not loyal to it

ex.en: Some disaffected members left to form a new party.
ex.cn: 部分不满的成员已脱党另立新党。

senses.def: to end the link between a group, a company or an organization and a larger one

ex.en: The local club has disaffiliated from the National Athletic Association.
ex.cn: 当地俱乐部已退出全国体育联合会。

senses.def: if two people disagree or one person disagrees with another about sth, they have a different opinion about it
senses.chn: 不同意；持不同意见；有分歧

ex.en: Even friends disagree sometimes.
ex.cn: 即便是朋友有时也有分歧。

ex.en: No, I disagree. I don't think it would be the right thing to do.
ex.cn: 不，我不赞成。我认为这样做不合适。

ex.en: He disagreed with his parents on most things.
ex.cn: 他在多数事情上都与父母意见不一。

ex.en: Some people disagree with this argument.
ex.cn: 有些人不同意这一论点。

ex.en: Few would disagree that students learn best when they are interested in the topic.
ex.cn: 学生对自己感兴趣的题目学得最好，这一点几乎所有人都不会有异议。

ex.en: I'm sorry, I don't agree/I have to disagree with you there.
ex.cn: 对不起，在那一点上我跟你有不同看法。

senses.def: if statements or reports disagree, they give different information
if sth, especially food, disagrees with you, it has a bad effect on you and makes you feel ill/sick
senses.chn: （尤指食物）对（某人）不适宜，使不舒服

senses.def: to believe that sth is bad or wrong; to disapprove of sth

ex.en: I disagree with violent protests.
ex.cn: 我不赞成暴力抗议。

senses.def: not nice or enjoyable
senses.chn: 不合意的；令人不快的；讨厌的

ex.en: a disagreeable smell/experience/job
ex.cn: 难闻的气味；令人不快的经历；不合意的工作

senses.def: rude and unfriendly

ex.en: a disagreeable bad-tempered man
ex.cn: 一个脾气不好难以相处的男人

senses.def: a situation where people have different opinions about sth and often argue

ex.en: Disagreement arose about exactly how to plan the show.
ex.cn: 在如何拟订具体演出计划的问题上出现了分歧。

ex.en: disagreement on the method to be used
ex.cn: 在要采用的方法上的争论

ex.en: There is considerable disagreement over the safety of the treatment.
ex.cn: 这种疗法是否安全争论很大。

ex.en: It was a source of disagreement between the two states.
ex.cn: 这就是两国纷争的一个根源。

ex.en: There is disagreement among archaeologists as to the age of the sculpture.
ex.cn: 考古学家在这尊雕塑的年代问题上意见不一。

ex.en: They have had several disagreements with their neighbours.
ex.cn: 他们与邻居发生过好几次争吵。

senses.def: a difference between two things that should be the same

ex.en: The comparison shows considerable disagreement between theory and practice.
ex.cn: 这一对比表明理论和实践之间有相当大的出入。

senses.def: if sth, especially food, disagrees with you, it has a bad effect on you and makes you feel ill/sick
senses.chn: （尤指食物）对（某人）不适宜，使不舒服

senses.def: to officially refuse to accept sth because it is not valid

ex.en: to disallow a claim/an appeal
ex.cn: 不接受要求；驳回上诉

ex.en: The second goal was disallowed.
ex.cn: 第二个进球被判无效。

senses.def: to show clearly the difference between two or more words, phrases, etc. which are similar in meaning
to become impossible to see

ex.en: The plane disappeared behind a cloud.
ex.cn: 飞机消失在云层里。

ex.en: Lisa watched until the train disappeared from view.
ex.cn: 莉萨一直看着火车从视线中消失。

senses.def: to stop existing

ex.en: Her nervousness quickly disappeared once she was on stage.
ex.cn: 她一走上台紧张情绪便迅速消失了。

ex.en: The problem won't just disappear.
ex.cn: 这个问题不会就这样不了了之的。

ex.en: Our countryside is disappearing at an alarming rate.
ex.cn: 我们的农村地区正在以惊人的速度消亡。

senses.def: to be lost or impossible to find

ex.en: I can never find a pen in this house. They disappear as soon as I buy them.
ex.cn: 我在家里从来找不到一支笔。每次我一买来就不翼而飞。

ex.en: The child disappeared from his home some time after four.
ex.cn: 这孩子四点多的时候就离家不见了。

senses.def: to go away or be impossible to find when people need or want you
to disappear completely
senses.chn: 完全消失；消逝得无影无踪

ex.en: Keep looking—they can't just have vanished off the face of the earth.
ex.cn: 继续找，他们不可能就从此消失得无影无踪的。

senses.def: to make sb feel sad because sth that they hope for or expect to happen does not happen or is not as good as they hoped

ex.en: Her decision to cancel the concert is bound to disappoint her fans.
ex.cn: 她决定取消这场音乐会，肯定会使她的歌迷失望。

ex.en: I hate to disappoint you, but I'm just not interested.
ex.cn: 我不想使你扫兴，但我确实不感兴趣。

ex.en: The movie had disappointed her (= it wasn't as good as she had expected).
ex.cn: 这部电影使她失望。

ex.en: His latest novel does not disappoint.
ex.cn: 他最近发表的这部小说没有使人失望。

senses.def: to prevent sth that sb hopes for from becoming a reality

ex.en: The new government had soon disappointed the hopes of many of its supporters.
ex.cn: 新政府不久便使许多支持者的希望破灭了。

senses.def: upset because sth you hoped for has not happened or been as good, successful, etc. as you expected

ex.en: They were bitterly disappointed at the result of the game.
ex.cn: 他们对比赛结果极为失望。

ex.en: I was disappointed by the quality of the wine.
ex.cn: 这酒的质量令我失望。

ex.en: I'm disappointed in you—I really thought I could trust you!
ex.cn: 你真让我失望，我原以为可以相信你的！

ex.en: I was very disappointed with myself.
ex.cn: 我对自己感到非常失望。

ex.en: He was disappointed to see she wasn't at the party.
ex.cn: 看到她没来参加晚会，他感到很失望。

ex.en: I'm disappointed (that) it was sold out.
ex.cn: 全都卖完了，我感到很失望。

senses.def: not as good, successful, etc. as you had hoped; making you feel disappointed
senses.chn: 令人失望的；令人沮丧的；令人扫兴的

ex.en: a disappointing result/performance
ex.cn: 令人失望的结果／演出

ex.en: The outcome of the court case was disappointing for the family involved.
ex.cn: 诉讼案的结果使得涉及本案的这家人非常失望。

senses.def: sadness because sth has not happened or been as good, successful, etc. as you expected or hoped

ex.en: Book early for the show to avoid disappointment.
ex.cn: 欲看演出，从速订票，以免向隅。

ex.en: To our great disappointment, it rained every day of the trip.
ex.cn: 这次旅行天天下雨，让我们大失所望。

ex.en: He found it difficult to hide his disappointment when she didn't arrive.
ex.cn: 她没有来，他感到很难掩饰自己内心的沮丧。

senses.def: a person or thing that is disappointing
senses.chn: 使人失望的人（或事物）；令人扫兴的人（或事物）

ex.en: a bitter/major disappointment
ex.cn: 令人极度失望／大失所望的事

ex.en: That new restaurant was a big disappointment.
ex.cn: 那家新餐馆使人大失所望。

ex.en: I always felt I was a disappointment to my father.
ex.cn: 我总觉得我使父亲失望了。

senses.def: disapproval of sb/sth that you think is morally wrong
senses.chn: （对不道德的人或事的）反对，不认可

senses.def: a feeling that you do not like an idea, an action or sb's behaviour because you think it is bad, not suitable or going to have a bad effect on sb else

ex.en: disapproval of his methods
ex.cn: 不赞同他的方法

ex.en: to show/express disapproval
ex.cn: 表明／表示反对

ex.en: He shook his head in disapproval.
ex.cn: 他摇了摇头，表示反对。

ex.en: She looked at my clothes with disapproval.
ex.cn: 她不满意地看着我的衣服。

senses.def: to think that sb/sth is not good or suitable; to not approve of sb/sth

ex.en: She wants to be an actress, but her parents disapprove.
ex.cn: 她想当演员，可是她父母不同意。

ex.en: He strongly disapproved of the changes that had been made.
ex.cn: 他强烈反对已进行的变革。

ex.en: A solid majority disapproves the way the president is handling the controversy.
ex.cn: 大多数人都反对总统处理争论的方式。

senses.def: showing that you do not approve of sb/sth
senses.chn: 不赞成的；表示反对的；不以为然的

ex.en: a disapproving glance/tone/look
ex.cn: 不以为然的一瞥／语气／样子

senses.def: to take a weapon or weapons away from sb
senses.chn: 缴（某人）的械；解除（某人）的武装

ex.en: Most of the rebels were captured and disarmed.
ex.cn: 大部分叛乱分子被俘获并解除了武装。

senses.def: to reduce the size of an army or to give up some or all weapons, especially nuclear weapons
senses.chn: 裁军；裁减军备（尤指核武器）

senses.def: to make sb feel less angry or critical
senses.chn: 消释（某人）的怒气（或批评）

ex.en: He disarmed her immediately by apologizing profusely.
ex.cn: 他一再向她道歉，很快便消解了她的怒气。

senses.def: the fact of a country reducing the size of its armed forces or the number of weapons, especially nuclear weapons, that it has
senses.chn: 裁军；裁减军备（尤指核武器）

ex.en: nuclear disarmament
ex.cn: 核裁军

ex.en: disarmament talks
ex.cn: 裁军谈判

senses.def: making people feel less angry or suspicious than they were before
senses.chn: 使人消气的；解人疑虑的

ex.en: a disarming smile
ex.cn: 使人消气的微笑

senses.def: to make sth untidy
a state of confusion and lack of organization in a situation or a place

ex.en: The peace talks broke up in disarray.
ex.cn: 和谈在混乱中破裂了。

ex.en: Our plans were thrown into disarray by her arrival.
ex.cn: 我们的计划因她的到来而陷入一片混乱。

senses.def: to take apart a machine or structure so that it is in separate pieces

ex.en: We had to completely disassemble the engine to find the problem.
ex.cn: 我们只好把发动机全部拆开以寻找故障原因。

senses.def: to translate sth from computer code into a language that can be read by humans
senses.chn: 反汇编（将计算机编码译成普通语言）

senses.def: to move apart and go away in different directions

ex.en: The concert ended and the crowd disassembled.
ex.cn: 音乐会结束，人群便散去了。

senses.def: a program used to disassemble (2) computer code
an unexpected event, such as a very bad accident, a flood or a fire, that kills a lot of people or causes a lot of damage

ex.en: an air disaster
ex.cn: 空难

ex.en: environmental disasters
ex.cn: 环境灾难

ex.en: Thousands died in the disaster.
ex.cn: 数千人在这场灾祸中丧生。

ex.en: a natural disaster (= one that is caused by nature)
ex.cn: 自然灾害

senses.def: a very bad situation that causes problems

ex.en: Losing your job doesn't have to be such a disaster.
ex.cn: 丢了工作不一定就是大难临头。

ex.en: Disaster struck when the wheel came off.
ex.cn: 车轮脱落，灾难就来了。

ex.en: financial disaster
ex.cn: 严重的财政危机

ex.en: Letting her organize the party is a recipe for disaster (= something that is likely to go badly wrong).
ex.cn: 让她来组织这次聚会非坏事不可。

senses.def: a complete failure

ex.en: As a teacher, he's a disaster.
ex.cn: 他当老师压根儿就不称职。

ex.en: The play's first night was a total disaster.
ex.cn: 这出戏头一晚就彻底演砸了。

senses.def: a thing or person that is very likely to cause danger or a problem in the future because of the condition it is in or the way they behave
a place where a disaster has happened and which needs special help
a place or situation that has a lot of problems, is a failure, or is badly organized
senses.chn: 问题成堆的地方；灾难性局面

senses.def: very bad, harmful or unsuccessful
senses.chn: 极糟糕的；灾难性的；完全失败的

ex.en: a disastrous harvest/fire/result
ex.cn: 严重歉收／火灾；灾难性的结果

ex.en: Lowering interest rates could have disastrous consequences for the economy.
ex.cn: 降低利率可能给经济带来灾难性后果。

senses.def: to state publicly that you have no knowledge of sth or that you are not responsible for sth/sb
senses.chn: 不承认；否认；拒绝对…承担责任

ex.en: They disavowed claims of a split in the party.
ex.cn: 他们否认了党内出现分裂的说法。

senses.def: to stop sb/sth from operating as a group; to separate or no longer operate as a group

ex.en: They set about disbanding the terrorist groups.
ex.cn: 他们开始解散恐怖主义组织。

ex.en: The committee formally disbanded in August.
ex.cn: 委员会于八月份正式解散。

senses.def: to stop a lawyer from working in the legal profession, especially because he or she has done sth illegal
the feeling of not being able to believe sth

ex.en: He stared at me in disbelief.
ex.cn: 他满腹疑惑地盯着我。

ex.en: To enjoy the movie you have to suspend your disbelief (= pretend to believe sth, even if it seems very unlikely).
ex.cn: 要欣赏这部电影就得暂且相信那甚至不可能发生的事。

senses.def: to not believe that sth is true or that sb is telling the truth

ex.en: Why should I disbelieve her story?
ex.cn: 我为什么要怀疑她的说法呢？

senses.def: to not believe that sth exists
to not believe that sth exists
to pay money to sb from a large amount that has been collected for a purpose
a thin flat round object

ex.en: He wears an identity disc around his neck.
ex.cn: 他脖子上挂着圆形身份牌。

senses.def: a disk for a computer
a structure made of cartilage between the bones of the back

ex.en: He's been off work with a slipped disc (= one that has moved from its correct position, causing pain).
ex.cn: 他因椎间盘突出一直未上班。

senses.def: to get rid of sth that you no longer want or need

ex.en: The room was littered with discarded newspapers.
ex.cn: 房间里到处是乱扔的报纸。

ex.en: He had discarded his jacket because of the heat.
ex.cn: 因天气炎热他脱掉了夹克。

ex.en: She could now discard all thought of promotion.
ex.cn: 她现在可以打消晋升的念头了。

ex.en: 10% of the data was discarded as unreliable.
ex.cn: 10% 的数据因不可靠而被废弃。

senses.def: to get rid of a card that you do not want
a person or thing that is not wanted or thrown away, especially a card in a card game
senses.chn: 被抛弃的人（或物）；（尤指纸牌游戏中）垫出的牌

senses.def: a brake that works by two surfaces pressing onto a disc in the centre of a wheel
to know, recognize or understand sth, especially sth that is not obvious

ex.en: It is possible to discern a number of different techniques in her work.
ex.cn: 从她的作品中可以辨别出许多不同的创作手法。

ex.en: He discerned a certain coldness in their welcome.
ex.cn: 他觉察到他们的接待有点冷淡。

ex.en: It is often difficult to discern how widespread public support is.
ex.cn: 了解公众支持的广泛程度常常是困难的。

ex.en: I quickly discerned that something was wrong.
ex.cn: 我很快觉察到出了问题。

senses.def: to see or hear sth, usually with difficulty

ex.en: We could just discern the house in the distance.
ex.cn: 我们只能勉强分辨出远处的房子。

senses.def: able to show good judgement about the quality of sb/sth
senses.chn: 有识别力的；有眼力的；有洞察力的

senses.def: the ability to show good judgement about the quality of sb/sth

ex.en: He shows great discernment in his choice of friends.
ex.cn: 他选择朋友很有眼光。

senses.def: to give sb official permission to leave a place or job; to make sb leave a job

ex.en: Patients were being discharged from the hospital too early.
ex.cn: 病人都过早获准出院。

ex.en: She had discharged herself against medical advice.
ex.cn: 她不听医嘱擅自出院了。

ex.en: He was discharged from the army following his injury.
ex.cn: 他受伤后就退伍了。

ex.en: She was discharged from the police force for bad conduct.
ex.cn: 她因行为不端被清除出警察队伍。

senses.def: to allow sb to leave prison or court

ex.en: He was conditionally discharged after admitting the theft.
ex.cn: 他承认偷盗行为后被有条件地释放了。

senses.def: when a gas or a liquid discharges or is discharged, or sb discharges it, it flows somewhere

ex.en: The river is diverted through the power station before discharging into the sea.
ex.cn: 这条河改道经水电站后流入大海。

ex.en: The factory was fined for discharging chemicals into the river.
ex.cn: 这家工厂因往河里排放化学物质而被罚款。

senses.def: to release force or power

ex.en: Lightning is caused by clouds discharging electricity.
ex.cn: 闪电是由云层放电产生的。

senses.def: to do everything that is necessary to perform and complete a particular duty

ex.en: to discharge your duties/responsibilities/obligations
ex.cn: 履行职责／责任／义务

ex.en: to discharge a debt (= to pay it)
ex.cn: 清偿债务

senses.def: to fire a gun, etc.
the action of releasing a substance such as a liquid or gas; a substance that comes out from inside somewhere

ex.en: a ban on the discharge of toxic waste
ex.cn: 禁止有毒废物的排放

ex.en: thunder and lightning caused by electrical discharges
ex.cn: 由放电产生的雷电

ex.en: nasal/vaginal discharge (= from the nose/ vagina )
ex.cn: 鼻涕；阴道分泌物

senses.def: the act of officially allowing sb, or of telling sb, to leave somewhere, especially sb in a hospital or the army
senses.chn: 获准离开；免职；出院；退伍

senses.def: the act of performing a task or a duty or of paying money that is owed
senses.chn: （任务或职责的）履行，执行；（债务的）清偿

ex.en: the discharge of debts/obligations
ex.cn: 债务的清偿；义务的履行

senses.def: a person who believes in and follows the teachings of a religious or political leader

ex.en: a disciple of the economist John Maynard Keynes
ex.cn: 经济学家约翰 · 梅纳德 · 凯恩斯的信徒

senses.def: (according to the Bible) one of the people who followed Jesus Christ and his teachings when he was living on earth, especially one of the twelve Apostles
a person who believes in using rules and punishments for controlling people
senses.chn: 严格纪律信奉者；严格执行纪律者

ex.en: She's a very strict disciplinarian.
ex.cn: 她执行纪律非常严格。

senses.def: connected with the punishment of people who break rules
senses.chn: 有关纪律的；执行纪律的；惩戒性的

ex.en: a disciplinary hearing (= to decide if sb has done sth wrong)
ex.cn: 纪律审讯

ex.en: The company will be taking disciplinary action against him.
ex.cn: 公司将对他进行纪律处分。

senses.def: the practice of training people to obey rules and orders and punishing them if they do not; the controlled behaviour or situation that results from this training

ex.en: The school has a reputation for high standards of discipline.
ex.cn: 这所学校因纪律严格而名闻遐迩。

ex.en: Strict discipline is imposed on army recruits.
ex.cn: 新兵受严格的纪律约束。

ex.en: She keeps good discipline in class.
ex.cn: 她严格执行课堂纪律。

senses.def: a method of training your mind or body or of controlling your behaviour; an area of activity where this is necessary
senses.chn: 训练方法；行为准则；符合准则的行为

ex.en: Yoga is a good discipline for learning to relax.
ex.cn: 瑜伽是一种学习放松的有效方法。

senses.def: the ability to control your behaviour or the way you live, work, etc.

ex.en: He'll never get anywhere working for himself—he's got no discipline.
ex.cn: 他自己做事是不会有什么成就的——他毫无自制力。

senses.def: an area of knowledge; a subject that people study or are taught, especially in a university
senses.chn: 知识领域；（尤指大学的）学科，科目

senses.def: to punish sb for sth they have done

ex.en: The officers were disciplined for using racist language.
ex.cn: 这些军官因使用种族歧视性语言而受到惩罚。

senses.def: to train sb, especially a child, to obey particular rules and control the way they behave

ex.en: a guide to the best ways of disciplining your child
ex.cn: 管教子女最佳方法指南

senses.def: to control the way you behave and make yourself do things that you believe you should do
senses.chn: 自我控制；严格要求（自己）

ex.en: Dieting is a matter of disciplining yourself.
ex.cn: 节食是自我控制的问题。

ex.en: He disciplined himself to exercise at least three times a week.
ex.cn: 他规定自己每周至少锻炼三次。

senses.def: a person whose job is to introduce and play recorded popular music, on radio or television or at a club
senses.chn: （电台、电视台、俱乐部）唱片节目主持人

senses.def: to state publicly that you have no knowledge of sth, or that you are not responsible for sth

ex.en: She disclaimed any knowledge of her husband's whereabouts.
ex.cn: 她否认知道丈夫的下落。

ex.en: The rebels disclaimed all responsibility for the explosion.
ex.cn: 叛乱分子否认对这次爆炸事件负有任何责任。

senses.def: to give up your right to sth, such as property or a title
senses.chn: 放弃（财产、头衔等的）权利

senses.def: a statement in which sb says that they are not connected with or responsible for sth, or that they do not have any knowledge of it
a statement in which a person says officially that they do not claim the right to do sth
to give sb information about sth, especially sth that was previously secret

ex.en: The spokesman refused to disclose details of the takeover to the press.
ex.cn: 发言人拒绝向新闻界透露公司收购的详细情况。

ex.en: The report discloses that human error was to blame for the accident.
ex.cn: 报告披露这次事故是人为原因造成的。

ex.en: It was disclosed that two women were being interviewed by the police.
ex.cn: 据透露，有两个女人当时正接受警方的问话。

ex.en: I cannot disclose what we discussed.
ex.cn: 我不能泄露我们讨论的内容。

senses.def: to allow sth that was hidden to be seen

ex.en: The door swung open, disclosing a long dark passage.
ex.cn: 门开了，露出一条昏暗的长通道。

senses.def: the act of making sth known or public that was previously secret or private

ex.en: the newspaper's disclosure of defence secrets
ex.cn: 报纸对防务内幕的披露

senses.def: information or a fact that is made known or public that was previously secret or private
senses.chn: 透露的秘闻；公开的事情；暴露的事实

ex.en: startling disclosures about his private life
ex.cn: 对他的私生活耸人听闻的披露

senses.def: a club or party where people dance to recorded pop music

ex.en: disco music/dancing
ex.cn: 迪斯科乐曲／舞

ex.en: the youth club disco
ex.cn: 青年俱乐部迪斯科舞厅

senses.def: the lights and sound equipment for such an event
senses.chn: 迪斯科舞会的灯光及音响设备

senses.def: all of the music that has been performed, written or collected by a particular person; a list of this music
senses.chn: （某人演唱、创作或收藏的）音乐作品集，音乐作品目录

senses.def: the study of musical recordings or collections
senses.chn: 音乐录音（或作品集）研究

senses.def: the process of becoming discoloured

ex.en: discoloration caused by the sun
ex.cn: 因日照引起的退色

senses.def: a place where sth has become discoloured
to change colour, or to make the colour of sth change, in a way that makes it look less attractive

ex.en: Plastic tends to discolour with age.
ex.cn: 塑料久而久之便会退色。

ex.en: The pipes were beginning to rust, discolouring the water.
ex.cn: 管子开始生锈，水都变颜色了。

senses.def: to make sb feel confused or embarrassed
a feeling of slight pain or of being physically uncomfortable
senses.chn: 轻微的病痛；不舒服；不适

ex.en: You will experience some minor discomfort during the treatment.
ex.cn: 治疗中你会稍感不适。

ex.en: abdominal discomfort
ex.cn: 腹部不适

senses.def: a feeling of worry or embarrassment

ex.en: John's presence caused her considerable discomfort.
ex.cn: 约翰在场使她颇感尴尬。

senses.def: something that makes you feel uncomfortable or causes you a slight feeling of pain
senses.chn: 使人不舒服的事物；苦事；痛苦

senses.def: to make sb feel anxious or embarrassed
senses.chn: 使不舒服；使不安；使尴尬

senses.def: to disturb sb and make them feel anxious
senses.chn: 扰乱；使不安；使心烦意乱

senses.def: to make sb feel anxious, confused or embarrassed

ex.en: His answer rather disconcerted her.
ex.cn: 他的回答使她颇感难堪。

senses.def: to remove a piece of equipment from a supply of gas, water or electricity
senses.chn: 切断（燃气、水或电的供应）

ex.en: First, disconnect the boiler from the water mains.
ex.cn: 先将锅炉与供水总管断开。

senses.def: to officially stop the supply of telephone lines, water, electricity or gas to a building
senses.chn: 切断（电话服务）；停止供应（水、电或燃气）

ex.en: You may be disconnected if you do not pay the bill.
ex.cn: 若不付账单就可能停止供应。

senses.def: to separate sth from sth

ex.en: The ski had become disconnected from the boot.
ex.cn: 滑雪板与靴子脱离了。

senses.def: to break the contact between two people who are talking on the telephone

ex.en: We were suddenly disconnected.
ex.cn: 我们的电话突然断了。

senses.def: to end a connection to the Internet

ex.en: I keep getting disconnected when I'm online.
ex.cn: 我连网时不断掉线。

ex.en: My computer crashes every time I disconnect from the Internet.
ex.cn: 我每次断网，计算机都会突然死机。

senses.def: not related to or connected with the things or people around
senses.chn: 分离的；断开的；无关联的

ex.en: disconnected images/thoughts/ideas
ex.cn: 互不相关的形象／思想／意见

ex.en: I felt disconnected from the world around me.
ex.cn: 我感到已与周围世界隔绝。

senses.def: with the parts not connected in a logical order
very unhappy and disappointed
senses.chn: 忧郁的；沮丧的；郁郁寡欢的

senses.def: a feeling of being unhappy because you are not satisfied with a particular situation; sth that makes you have this feeling
senses.chn: 不满；不满足；不满足的缘由

ex.en: There is widespread discontent among the staff at the proposed changes to pay and conditions.
ex.cn: 员工对改变工资和工作环境的建议普遍不满。

senses.def: unhappy because you are not satisfied with your situation
to stop doing, using or providing sth, especially sth that you have been doing, using or providing regularly

ex.en: It was decided to discontinue the treatment after three months.
ex.cn: 决定三个月后终止治疗。

senses.def: to stop making a product

ex.en: a sale of discontinued china
ex.cn: 出售已停止生产的瓷器

senses.def: the state of not being continuous

ex.en: discontinuity in the children's education
ex.cn: 儿童教育的不连贯性

senses.def: a break or change in a continuous process

ex.en: Changes in government led to discontinuities in policy.
ex.cn: 政府的更迭导致政策缺乏连续性。

senses.def: not continuous; stopping and starting again
senses.chn: 不连续的；间断的；断续的

senses.def: disagreement; arguing

ex.en: marital/family discord
ex.cn: 夫妻／家庭不和

ex.en: A note of discord surfaced during the proceedings.
ex.cn: 事件进程中出现了不和的征兆。

senses.def: a combination of musical notes that do not sound pleasant together
not in agreement; combining with other things in a way that is strange or unpleasant
senses.chn: 不一致的；不协调的；不和的

ex.en: discordant views
ex.cn: 相互冲突的观点

senses.def: not sounding pleasant together
an amount of money that is taken off the usual cost of sth

ex.en: to get/give/offer a discount
ex.cn: 得到／给予／提供折扣

ex.en: discount rates/prices
ex.cn: 贴现率；折扣价

ex.en: They're offering a 10% discount on all sofas this month.
ex.cn: 本月他们给沙发售价统统打九折。

ex.en: They were selling everything at a discount (= at reduced prices).
ex.cn: 他们销售的所有商品都打折。

ex.en: a discount shop (= one that regularly sells goods at reduced prices)
ex.cn: 打折商店

ex.en: Do you give any discount?
ex.cn: 你们打折吗？

senses.def: to think or say that sth is not important or not true
senses.chn: 认为…不重要；对…不全信；低估

ex.en: We cannot discount the possibility of further strikes.
ex.cn: 我们不能低估再次发生罢工的可能性。

ex.en: The news reports were being discounted as propaganda.
ex.cn: 人们认为这些新闻报道不过是为了宣传，不可全信。

senses.def: to take an amount of money off the usual cost of sth; to sell sth at a discount

ex.en: discounted prices/fares
ex.cn: 打折价／票价

senses.def: a shop/store that sells things very cheaply, often in large quantities or from a limited range of goods
the minimum rate of interest that banks in the US and some other countries must pay when they borrow money from other banks
senses.chn: （美国及其他一些国家银行之间借款的）贴现率

senses.def: the amount that the price of a bill of exchange is reduced by when it is bought before it reaches its full value
the rate at which an investment increases in value each year
to try to prevent sth or to prevent sb from doing sth, especially by making it difficult to do or by showing that you do not approve of it

ex.en: a campaign to discourage smoking among teenagers
ex.cn: 劝阻青少年吸烟的运动

ex.en: I leave a light on when I'm out to discourage burglars.
ex.cn: 我出门时开着灯以防夜贼闯入。

ex.en: His parents tried to discourage him from being an actor.
ex.cn: 他的父母试图阻止他去当演员。

senses.def: to make sb feel less confident or enthusiastic about doing sth
senses.chn: 使灰心；使泄气；使丧失信心

ex.en: Don't be discouraged by the first failure—try again!
ex.cn: 这才是第一次失败，别灰心丧气，再试一次吧！

ex.en: The weather discouraged people from attending.
ex.cn: 这天气使得人们不愿到场出席。

senses.def: a feeling that you no longer have the confidence or enthusiasm to do sth

ex.en: an atmosphere of discouragement and despair
ex.cn: 灰心绝望的气氛

senses.def: the action of trying to stop sth

ex.en: the government's discouragement of political protest
ex.cn: 政府对政治抗议的阻拦

senses.def: a thing that discourages sb from doing sth

ex.en: Despite all these discouragements, she refused to give up.
ex.cn: 尽管遇到这么多挫折，她仍不气馁。

senses.def: a long and serious treatment or discussion of a subject in speech or writing

ex.en: a discourse on issues of gender and sexuality
ex.cn: 关于性别和性行为的论文

ex.en: He was hoping for some lively political discourse at the meeting.
ex.cn: 他希望在会上听到些生动的政治演讲。

senses.def: the use of language in speech and writing in order to produce meaning; language that is studied, usually in order to see how the different parts of a text are connected

ex.en: spoken/written discourse
ex.cn: 口头／书面语篇

ex.en: discourse analysis
ex.cn: 语篇分析

senses.def: to talk or give a long speech about sth that you know a lot about
a word or phrase that organizes spoken language into different parts, for example 'Well…' or 'On the other hand…'
having bad manners and not showing respect for other people
senses.chn: 不礼貌的；失礼的；粗鲁的

ex.en: Why are you so rude to your mother?
ex.cn: 你为什么对你的母亲这么没礼貌？

ex.en: It's rude to speak when you're eating.
ex.cn: 吃东西时说话不礼貌。

ex.en: You cheeky monkey!
ex.cn: 你这厚脸皮的猴崽子！

ex.en: a cheeky grin
ex.cn: 厚颜无耻的龇牙一笑

ex.en: Some people said he had been disrespectful to the President in his last speech.
ex.cn: 有些人说他在最近一次讲话中对总统不尊重。

ex.en: Some people think it is impolite to ask someone's age.
ex.cn: 有些人认为询问别人的年龄是不礼貌的。

senses.def: behaviour or an action that is not polite
senses.chn: 失礼的行为；粗鲁的举动

senses.def: to be the first person to become aware that a particular place or thing exists

ex.en: Cook is credited with discovering Hawaii.
ex.cn: 人们把发现夏威夷的功劳归于库克。

ex.en: Scientists around the world are working to discover a cure for AIDS.
ex.cn: 全世界的科学家都在努力寻找治疗艾滋病的方法。

senses.def: to find sb/sth that was hidden or that you did not expect to find

ex.en: Police discovered a large stash of drugs while searching the house.
ex.cn: 警方搜查这栋房子时发现里面藏着一大批毒品。

ex.en: We discovered this beach while we were sailing around the island.
ex.cn: 我们在围绕这个海岛航行时发现了这个海滩。

ex.en: He was discovered hiding in a shed.
ex.cn: 人们发现他原来藏在棚屋里。

ex.en: She was discovered dead at her home in Leeds.
ex.cn: 人们发现她死在利兹的家里。

senses.def: to find out about sth; to find some information about sth

ex.en: I've just discovered hang-gliding!
ex.cn: 我刚知道有悬挂式滑翔运动！

ex.en: It was a shock to discover (that) he couldn't read.
ex.cn: 得知他不识字真令人震惊。

ex.en: We never did discover why she gave up her job.
ex.cn: 我们一直弄不清楚她为什么辞职。

ex.en: It was later discovered that the diaries were a fraud.
ex.cn: 后来查明这些日记完全是伪造的。

ex.en: He was later discovered to be seriously ill.
ex.cn: 后来才了解到他患了重病。

senses.def: to be the first person to realize that sb is very good at singing, acting, etc. and help them to become successful and famous

ex.en: The singer was discovered while still at school.
ex.cn: 这个歌唱家在上学的时候就受到赏识了。

senses.def: that you can find by searching or find easily
an act or the process of finding sb/sth, or learning about sth that was not known about before

ex.en: the discovery of antibiotics in the 20th century
ex.cn: 20 世纪抗生素的发现

ex.en: The discovery of a child's body in the river has shocked the community.
ex.cn: 在河里发现一个孩子的尸体，使社区大为震惊。

ex.en: the discovery of new talent in the art world
ex.cn: 艺术界新秀的发现

ex.en: Researchers in this field have made some important new discoveries.
ex.cn: 这个领域的研究人员有了一些重大的新发现。

ex.en: He saw life as a voyage of discovery.
ex.cn: 他把生命看作是一次探索未知世界的航行。

ex.en: She was shocked by the discovery that he had been unfaithful.
ex.cn: 她发觉他不忠时感到非常震惊。

senses.def: a thing, fact or person that is found or learned about for the first time
senses.chn: 被发现的事物（或真相、人）

ex.en: The drug is not a new discovery—it's been known about for years.
ex.cn: 这种药并不是什么新发现，多年前便为人所知。

senses.def: to make people stop respecting sb/sth
senses.chn: 败坏…的名声；使丧失信誉；使丢脸

ex.en: The photos were deliberately taken to discredit the President.
ex.cn: 这些蓄意拍摄的照片旨在败坏总统的名声。

ex.en: a discredited government/policy
ex.cn: 名声扫地的政府；失去信誉的政策

senses.def: to make people stop believing that sth is true; to make sth appear unlikely to be true
senses.chn: 使不相信；使怀疑；使不可置信

ex.en: These theories are now largely discredited among linguists.
ex.cn: 这些理论现已大多受到语言学家的质疑。

senses.def: damage to sb's reputation; loss of respect
senses.chn: 名誉丧失；信誉丧失；丢脸

ex.en: Violent football fans bring discredit on the teams they support.
ex.cn: 狂暴的足球迷败坏了他们所支持球队的声誉。

ex.en: Britain, to its discredit, did not speak out against these atrocities.
ex.cn: 英国没有公开反对这些残暴行为，因而名誉扫地。

senses.def: bad and unacceptable; causing people to lose respect
senses.chn: 不光彩的；有损尊严的；丢脸的

senses.def: careful in what you say or do, in order to keep sth secret or to avoid causing embarrassment or difficulty for sb
senses.chn: （言行）谨慎的，慎重的；考虑周到的

ex.en: He was always very discreet about his love affairs.
ex.cn: 他对两性关系一贯谨小慎微。

ex.en: You ought to make a few discreet enquiries before you sign anything.
ex.cn: 你应该审慎地询问清楚再签字。

senses.def: a difference between two or more things that should be the same

ex.en: wide discrepancies in prices quoted for the work
ex.cn: 这项工作的报价出入很大

ex.en: What are the reasons for the discrepancy between girls' and boys' performance in school?
ex.cn: 女生和男生在学校表现不同的原因何在呢？

senses.def: independent of other things of the same type

ex.en: The organisms can be divided into discrete categories.
ex.cn: 有机体可分为许多互不关联的种类。

senses.def: the freedom or power to decide what should be done in a particular situation
senses.chn: 自行决定的自由；自行决定权

ex.en: I'll leave it up to you to use your discretion.
ex.cn: 我把这件事留给你自己斟酌决定。

ex.en: How much to tell terminally ill patients is left to the discretion of the doctor.
ex.cn: 晚期病人的病情让本人知道多少由医生自行决定。

senses.def: care in what you say or do, in order to keep sth secret or to avoid causing embarrassment to or difficulty for sb; the quality of being discreet

ex.en: This is confidential, but I know that I can rely on your discretion.
ex.cn: 这是机密，不过我知道你靠得住。

senses.def: according to what sb decides or wishes to do
senses.chn: 由某人斟酌决定；按照某人的意愿

ex.en: Bail is granted at the discretion of the court.
ex.cn: 由法庭决定准予保释。

ex.en: There is no service charge and tipping is at your discretion.
ex.cn: 不收服务费，给不给小费由你自行决定。

senses.def: you should avoid danger and not take unnecessary risks
senses.chn: 谨慎即大勇；慎重为勇敢之本

senses.def: decided according to the judgement of a person in authority about what is necessary in each particular situation; not decided by rules
senses.chn: 自行决定的；酌情行事的；便宜行事的

ex.en: You may be eligible for a discretionary grant for your university course.
ex.cn: 读大学课程可能会有资格获得学校自行决定是否发放的助学金。

discretion is the better part of valour.lemma: discretion is the better part of valour

senses.def: you should avoid danger and not take unnecessary risks
senses.chn: 谨慎即大勇；慎重为勇敢之本

senses.def: to recognize that there is a difference between people or things; to show a difference between people or things

ex.en: The computer program was unable to discriminate between letters and numbers.
ex.cn: 这计算机程序不能辨别字母与数字。

ex.en: When do babies learn to discriminate voices?
ex.cn: 婴儿什么时候学会辨别嗓音呢？

ex.en: A number of features discriminate this species from others.
ex.cn: 有些特征使这一物种与其他物种区别开来。

senses.def: to treat one person or group worse/better than another in an unfair way

ex.en: practices that discriminate against women and in favour of men
ex.cn: 重男轻女的做法

ex.en: It is illegal to discriminate on grounds of race, sex or religion.
ex.cn: 因种族、性别或宗教信仰而实行歧视是非法的。

senses.def: able to judge the good quality of sth
senses.chn: 有识别力的；有辨别力的；有鉴赏力的

ex.en: a discriminating audience/customer
ex.cn: 有鉴赏力的观众／顾客

senses.def: the practice of treating sb or a particular group in society less fairly than others

ex.en: age/racial/sex/sexual discrimination (= because of sb's age, race or sex)
ex.cn: 年龄／种族／性别歧视

ex.en: discrimination against the elderly
ex.cn: 歧视老人

ex.en: discrimination in favour of the young
ex.cn: 厚待年轻人

ex.en: discrimination on the grounds of race, gender, or sexual orientation
ex.cn: 按照种族、性别或性取向给予区别对待

senses.def: the ability to judge what is good, true, etc.

ex.en: He showed great discrimination in his choice of friends.
ex.cn: 他在择友方面颇具慧眼。

senses.def: the ability to recognize a difference between one thing and another; a difference that is recognized

ex.en: to learn discrimination between right and wrong
ex.cn: 学会分辨是非

ex.en: fine discriminations
ex.cn: 细微区别

senses.def: unfair; treating sb or one group of people worse than others
senses.chn: 区别对待的；不公正的；歧视的

ex.en: discriminatory practices/rules/measures
ex.cn: 不公正的做法／规定／措施

ex.en: sexually/racially discriminatory laws
